FreshJournal is sealed and fail-closed: verification rejects indirect journal files, owner mismatch, non-newline-terminated event tails, malformed envelopes, sequence/previous-hash/hash-chain violations, replay-invalid event semantics and head sequence/hash mismatch. append() verifies existing authority first, validates the prospective event before writing, fsyncs the event stream, atomically replaces the sealed head, then re-verifies; an interrupted or inconsistent transaction poisons or fails reopening rather than resetting history.

Existing tests exercise truncation, complete-tail deletion, schema/content tampering, missing head, owner mismatch, recomputed semantic-invalid attempts, disk-write failure, byte-exact restart replay and single-writer behavior. No journal integrity defect was found under the documented fail-closed rather than guaranteed power-loss-recovery model.

Checkpoint creation first invokes journal.verify() under the FreshRequests lock and derives only immutable wire requests from the replayed records. Python restart reconstructs records without dispatch, leaves active unset, preserves journal bytes, and requires explicit retry to append a new attempt.

Background restart is also non-sending: fresh_welcome calls restore(checkpoint) and status() only; restore validates checkpoint schema/protocol/delivery semantics, individual request contracts, duplicate attempt keys and logical identity conflicts, replaces only the expendable session mirror and never calls dispatch. The cross-language restart test confirms cache loss restores the Python checkpoint while emitting no C2C_FRESH_REVIEW, navigation, injection or recovery action.
